A new function, `font_errors(root, paths)`, checks every delivered `.ttf`, `.otf`, `.ttc`, `.woff` and `.woff2` file:
  - Any font at another path fails.
  - The approved font must match its recorded bytes exactly.
  - The license must be in the same delivered set (being on disk isn't enough) and must match its recorded hash.

  `private_path`, `handoff_files` and `delivery_files` are unchanged, and no font is hidden from any inventory.
- **License line endings**: the license file in the worktree uses CRLF on all 93 lines (checked with Grep only). The recorded hash is therefore of the CRLF bytes, while `.gitattributes` will check the file out as LF. Before hashing, the check converts CRLF to LF and then back to CRLF. So both forms match the recorded hash without any new constant, and any text change or stray CR still fails. If Root prefers an LF-based SHA constant, only that one value needs replacing.
- **`tools/ai/test_handoff.py`**: I renamed the failing test to `test_only_approved_licensed_font_and_no_credentials_shipped`. It now requires `font_errors == []`, and the private-path check still runs on every file, including the font.

- **`tests/test_delivery_files.py`**: existing tests are untouched. The new tests read the real font and license bytes from the repo and use only temporary roots. They cover:
  - the approved font with the license in either CRLF or LF form passes;
  - unapproved font paths fail: a moved copy, a `.OTF` and a `.woff2`;
  - an altered font binary fails;
  - a missing, altered or gitignored (not delivered) license fails;
  - the error cap works;
  - a successful manifest records the font's exact SHA;
